articles.title: Ancient inscription
articles.description: A damaged inscription discovered beneath the First Forge describes the Ladder as revealing what pressure has made rather than crowning the worthy. Another fragment refers to recognition of the Eight; its remaining text is missing.

articles.title: Bloodied Daggers
articles.description: A Bloodied Dagger is a serialized wagered dagger enhanced through its first Bold victory. Further victories add Prestige at Fibonacci milestones, with no hard cap. Progress belongs to the exact dagger: transfer preserves it and defeat does not reset it.

articles.title: Crucible Daggers
articles.description: Crucible awards use Emerald daggers with Bronze, Silver and Gold base Prestige of 9, 11 and 13; Dragonsteel equivalents carry 10, 13 and 16. Participation has base Prestige 1. Season II does not award relegation daggers.

articles.title: Daggers
articles.description: Competitive daggers are physical records of achievements, ownership and competitive history in Aetherforge.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: A dagger carries the identity and accomplishments of its owner. Daggersmiths engrave, craft and maintain these objects; the Council safeguards competitive records.

content.heading: FYI awards and game systems
content.body: FYI league and game systems distinguish daggers by award, competitive achievement, provenance and wager history. These rules are separate from the physical nature of daggers in the fictional setting.

articles.title: Division Daggers
articles.description: Division Daggers are competitive artifacts associated with a contender’s progression through the Ladder.

content.heading: Tradition
content.body: At Ignition, entrants receive a blank dagger to be personalized by a daggersmith. Lilith Vanthe forges her own Division Dagger.

articles.title: Dragonsteel Daggers
articles.description: Weekly Dragonsteel awards recognize Bold wins: Bronze at one, Silver at three and Gold for the most wins. The awards stack, and a 2v2 win counts twice. Generations explicitly awards Gold to all golfers tied for the weekly lead.

articles.title: Golden Crucible Dagger
articles.description: The Golden Crucible Dagger is an award for victory in a Crucible. Lilith Vanthe received one before entering Ignition.

articles.title: Identifier 117-3A
articles.description: 117-3A is an identifier recorded in ancient archives and associated with Rheon Valek’s modern credential. The relationship between the historical and modern records is unresolved.

articles.title: Kharadon’s Crown
articles.description: Kharadon’s Crown is a FYI Guilds standings award for the guild with the best cumulative raw score across all finishers.

content.heading: Award
content.body: Under Season 1 rules the award grants five standings points. Tie treatment is not specified.

articles.title: Kharadon's seal
articles.description: Kharadon’s seal is a seven-pointed forge-star surrounding a central flame. It is present in ancient infrastructure beneath the First Forge.

articles.title: Kickoff Dagger
articles.description: The Season 2 Kickoff Dagger is a non-wagerable commemorative award with zero Prestige. It is granted once to simulated FYI members present in the entry snapshot, excluding visiting outsiders.

articles.title: Kingdom Seals
articles.description: Kingdom Seals are FYI Guilds awards recognizing individual performance, collective mastery and roster participation. They award additional standings points under the applicable season rules.

content.heading: Dominion
content.body: Five points for an event winner, or three for a top-five finisher when the guild has no winner.

content.heading: Precision
content.body: Three points when at least one-third of the roster, rounded up, finishes within ten strokes of the leader.

content.heading: Mastery
content.body: Three points when at least half the roster, rounded up, finishes in the top half of the field.

content.heading: Flame
content.body: Three points when at least 40% of the roster, rounded up, finishes at −40 or better under the Season 1 scoring specification.

content.heading: Roster completion (Endurance / Cinder)
content.body: Three points at 85% roster completion or five points for full completion. This seal is also known as Cinder or Endurance.

content.heading: Unbroken
content.body: At least 85% of the roster must complete the event. The best two scores outside the top twelve count; with exactly thirteen finishers, use the thirteenth score, and with exactly twelve eligible finishers, use the twelfth. The lowest eligible total earns five points; tied guilds all win.

articles.title: Legendary daggers
articles.description: Legendary significance may arise from extraordinary workmanship, exceptional materials, dragon recognition or the achievements of a wielder. These four paths can accumulate on a single dagger in the game design.

articles.title: Participation Daggers
articles.description: Competitors earn one Participation Dagger for completing three society events in an eligible week through week six. Playoff weeks and non-division entrants are included.

articles.title: Placement Daggers
articles.description: Placement Daggers are reserved for divisional entrants in standalone Season 1. Base Prestige rises by division: Ashen 2, Cinder 4, Ember 6, Damascus 8, Titanium 10 and Obsidian 12.

articles.title: Playoff Daggers
articles.description: Each playoff qualifier receives one gold-handled dagger. The award progression is Pearl (3 Prestige), Lapis Lazuli (5), Opal (8), Moonstone (12), Amethyst (16), Topaz (22), Sapphire (40), Ruby (55) and Diamond (70).

articles.title: The Ashen Reach
articles.description: The Ashen Reach is a dark-metal dagger with a split guard and an inscription. Disagreement between its display and archival dates makes it significant to the Council’s investigation of the realm’s historical records.

articles.title: Unbroken Star
articles.description: The Unbroken Star is associated in tradition with Kael Varen, the earliest contender to complete the Ladder. Whether the name refers to a physical artifact remains unknown.

articles.title: Aeren Vale
articles.description: Aeren Vale is an Ash-born golfer, the son of Ellen and Draven Vale and a member of the Eight.

content.heading: Family and identity
content.body: Aeren belongs to House Vale, a family associated with resilience and the legendary champion Lyra Vale. He seeks recognition independent of the family name.

content.heading: Associations
content.body: Torrick Drake is his friend and Cassian Rourke is a competitive rival.

articles.title: Aric Flare
articles.description: Aric Flare, remembered as the Ember Wolf, is associated with House Flare and the pursuit of stronger opponents. His disappearance remains unexplained.

articles.title: Bustin
articles.description: Bustin is a founding member of the Administrative Council, known as the Forge Engineer and Architect of the Forge.

content.heading: Responsibilities
content.body: A Titanium native with Ember competitive affiliation, he oversees the realm’s technical infrastructure and investigates unusual activity in its competitive systems.

articles.title: Caelor Rhyne
articles.description: Caelor Rhyne, the Silver Measure, is remembered for exact execution.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: Caelor’s victories exemplify exact execution rather than overwhelming force. Aurelith reportedly praised him as “Precise,” regarded as extraordinary praise in Titanium.

articles.title: Cassian Rourke
articles.description: Cassian Rourke is a golfer known for powerful, aggressive play and his competitive rivalry with Aeren Vale.

articles.title: Corin Thale
articles.description: Corin Thale is a golfer associated with Ignition.

articles.title: Darian Vex
articles.description: Darian Vex was a contender from House Vex associated with opposition to Kharadon’s control of access to the Summit.

content.heading: Historical accounts
content.body: Accounts describe a reform grievance that developed into a struggle for supremacy. Official history records his death at the Broken Summit, although traditions about his fate diverge.

articles.title: Draven Vale
articles.description: Draven Vale, known competitively as Daggs, comes from a wealthy Obsidian family. He became Travis Pope’s caddie after Travis qualified for Ash. He married Ellen, adopted her surname and is Aeren Vale’s father.

articles.title: Edric Mourn
articles.description: Edric Mourn is associated with archival research at Vaelorian Citadel and the investigation of historical records.

articles.title: Elias Kest
articles.description: Elias Kest is a golfer who represents Titanium at Ignition.

articles.title: Ellen Vale
articles.description: Ellen Vale is an Ash-born golfer, Lilith Vanthe’s lifelong caddie and strategic partner, and the mother of Aeren Vale.

content.heading: Partnership
content.body: Ellen met Lilith while competing in Ember and became her caddie. Their partnership centers on course management and analysis.

content.heading: Family
content.body: Ellen married Draven, who adopted the Vale surname. Their son is Aeren Vale.

articles.title: Jalen Marr
articles.description: Jalen Marr is a golfer associated with the Ignition competition.

articles.title: Kael Varen
articles.description: Kael Varen is remembered as the first mortal to complete the Ladder and reach Kharadon’s Summit. Accounts of his subsequent fate disagree.

content.heading: First Ascension
content.body: The official chronology generally dates Kael’s First Ascension to 103 AL, although surviving records of his advancement through the six kingdoms are fragmentary. Tradition describes him as entering Ignition without kingdom allegiance or celebrated lineage and discovering that the Summit lay beyond Obsidian.

content.heading: Historical traditions
content.body: Accounts agree that Kael became the First Ascendant but differ on whether he retired, disappeared, died or remained silent afterward. A later descent is absent from the familiar account.

articles.title: Kaelen Rhyne
articles.description: Kaelen Rhyne is a golfer and member of the Eight.

articles.title: Kira
articles.description: Kira is an Ember-born smith from a family of modest means who aspires to master her craft.

content.heading: Family and background
content.body: Her older sister Mara is a locally respected smith, her father works in mining, and she has three younger brothers.

articles.title: Lauren
articles.description: Lauren, alias Stick, is a male golfer from a wealthy Obsidian family and a friend of Travis and Draven. He initially enters Ignition as a competitor rather than an established caddie.

articles.title: Lilith Vanthe
articles.description: Lilith Vanthe, also known as Lily and competitively as Pretty, is an Ash-born daggersmith, Obsidian golfer and founding member of the Administrative Council.

content.heading: Early life
content.body: Born Lyra Northashe and named after Lyra Vale, Lilith began smithcraft at twelve and became financially independent at fifteen. She learned golf through clients and entered Ignition at seventeen.

content.heading: Competitive career
content.body: Lilith won a Crucible before entering Ignition. She advanced quickly through Ash before facing a more demanding field in Cinder. Her accurate play eventually carried her to Obsidian, where she continued competing during Council service.

content.heading: Craftsmanship
content.body: Lilith owns a forge in Ash. She forged her own Division Dagger and irons with obsidian heads, golden shafts and leather grips.

content.heading: Professional associations
content.body: Ellen Vale is her caddie and strategic partner. Travis Pope and Rowden Groves are fellow competitors.

content.heading: Council service
content.body: As the Daggersmith and Dragon’s Ascension Administrator, she oversees divisions, standings, head-to-head competition and daggers.

articles.title: Lyra (Acolyte12)
articles.description: Lyra, known as Acolyte12, is the Founder of FYI, Sorceress Supreme and a founding member of the Administrative Council.

content.heading: Leadership
content.body: An Obsidian native competing in Damascus, Lyra founded FYI and guides the Administrative Council’s overall direction.

articles.title: Lyra Vale
articles.description: Lyra Vale, remembered as the Ashborn, is a legendary champion whose career embodies Ash’s philosophy of recovery.

content.heading: Legacy
content.body: Tradition recalls eleven early challenge losses before her emergence as a champion. Her legacy is expressed in the words “The fall is not the end.” Lilith Vanthe was originally named Lyra Northashe in her honor.

articles.title: Maera Sol
articles.description: Maera Sol is a postwar champion whose repeated rebuilding symbolizes Ash resilience and Obsidian achievement.

articles.title: Malrek Voss
articles.description: Malrek Voss, the Obsidian Crown, is remembered as a conqueror of the Ladder who never completed the Summit.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: Malrek is remembered for an unprecedented undefeated period in Obsidian; despite conquering the Ladder, he never completed the Summit.

articles.title: Mira Ardyn
articles.description: Mira Ardyn is a golfer and member of the Eight.

articles.title: Nyra Solvar
articles.description: Nyra Solvar is a golfer and member of the Eight. She is characterized by an aggressive approach to opportunity and risk.

articles.title: Orin Cade
articles.description: Orin Cade is a golfer whose competitive style emphasizes consistency and a disciplined routine.

articles.title: PJ
articles.description: PJ is a founding member of the Administrative Council and holds the title Vaelorian Seer.

content.heading: Responsibilities
content.body: A Damascus native who competes in Obsidian, PJ oversees accuracy, quality control and consistency.

articles.title: Rheon Valek
articles.description: Rheon Valek is a golfer and member of the Eight, associated with the unexplained credential identifier 117-3A.

articles.title: Rowden Groves
articles.description: Rowden Groves is a Cinder golfer and competitive acquaintance of Lilith Vanthe.

content.heading: Career and craft
content.body: Rowden advanced through Cinder and has an interest in smithcraft. His irons have bronze shafts and Cinderian brimstone heads.

articles.title: Selene Ardyn
articles.description: Selene Ardyn, the Damascus Hand, is remembered as a legendary strategist and craftmaster who adapts between contests.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: Selene’s ability to reinvent her approach between contests made her difficult to prepare against. Tradition alleges Seraphyne granted her access to Damascus’s deepest chambers.

articles.title: Sera Voss
articles.description: Sera Voss is a golfer associated with House Voss and a member of the Eight. Her playing style emphasizes precision and consistency.

articles.title: Soulless
articles.description: Soulless is a founding member of the Administrative Council and holds the title Master of the Inferno.

content.heading: Responsibilities
content.body: An Ember native who competes in Obsidian, he oversees team competition, captains and matchups.

articles.title: Tessa Brann
articles.description: Tessa Brann is a golfer and member of the Eight.

articles.title: Torren Drake
articles.description: Torren Drake, the Last Cinder, is remembered for the longest recorded Cinder campaign.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: Torren’s reputation comes from surviving the longest recorded Cinder campaign despite not being considered naturally gifted; Drakhar reportedly watched his final contest.

articles.title: Torrick Drake
articles.description: Torrick Drake is a Cinder contender, friend of Aeren Vale and member of the Eight.

articles.title: Travis Pope
articles.description: Travis Pope, known competitively as TPope, is an Obsidian-born golfer and friend of Lilith Vanthe.

content.heading: Competition
content.body: A wealthy prodigy close to Lilith’s age, Travis travels for Crucibles and knows her from Ash-hosted competitions.

articles.title: Vanthe Plouffe
articles.description: Vanthe Plouffe was a former partner of Lilith Vanthe who adopted Crownless ideology and attacked her. Lilith killed Vanthe in self-defense.

articles.title: Vela Sorn
articles.description: Vela Sorn is a golfer associated with Ignition.

articles.title: Whiskey
articles.description: Whiskey is a founding member of the Administrative Council and holds the title Aetherforge Sentinel.

content.heading: Responsibilities
content.body: A Cinder native with Titanium competitive affiliation, he protects community standards and helps maintain order during competitive events.

articles.title: Aetherforge Inferno
articles.description: The Aetherforge Inferno is FYI’s team competition, overseen by Soulless, the Master of the Inferno.

content.heading: Purpose
content.body: It emphasizes coordination, trust and leadership among contenders.

articles.title: Bold challenges
articles.description: In a one-on-one Bold Challenge, the winner keeps the wagered dagger and captures the loser's. Teams in two-on-two play are randomized, and each winning dagger receives two Bold wins. Losing daggers are selected according to winning-wager Prestige, then signup order.

articles.title: Christmas exhibition
articles.description: The Christmas Exhibition is the week-five special event of FYI Guilds Season 1. It recognizes the best individual performance and best cumulative guild score without awarding regular-season standings or Seal points.

articles.title: Crucibles
articles.description: Crucibles are longstanding competitive tournaments that predate FYI and the Administrative Council.

content.heading: Tradition
content.body: Crucibles allow contenders to distinguish themselves outside ordinary divisional competition. The strongest competitors tend to come from the upper divisions.

articles.title: Direct challenges
articles.description: Direct Challenges permit multiple daggers of unequal value to be wagered. Ownership transfers on a loss, but Direct wins do not advance Bloodied progression. Winning teammates alternate picks from the losing pool.

articles.title: Division movement
articles.description: The top two competitors promote and the bottom two relegate where a neighboring division exists. Event podium daggers use two-round aggregate results, with competition-ranking ties.

content.heading: Generations rules
content.body: In the standalone simulation, main-league rosters change only during the offseason. Departures create no-show losses while records and inactive identities persist; vacancies cascade upward, with further generalization still open.

articles.title: Dragon’s Ascension
articles.description: Dragon’s Ascension is FYI’s individual league competition, distinct from the team-based Inferno.

content.heading: Divisional structure
content.body: The league is organized around the six divisions of the Ladder, with movement between divisions based on performance.

content.heading: Season II
content.body: The Trial of Blades is the final Crown event in the Season II league rules.

articles.title: Dragon’s Ascension: Generations
articles.description: Dragon’s Ascension: Generations is a simulated golf career manager set in fictional FYI.

content.heading: Career
content.body: Golfers compete across six divisions, advance or relegate, build careers and collect daggers. Results come from the simulation rather than real-world player performance. Collectible daggers do not improve golfer skill.

content.heading: Competition systems
content.body: The game includes regular divisional competition, Crucibles, the Trial of Blades, Bold matches through the Ironbound Arena and inter-society invitationals.

content.heading: Calendar
content.body: A repeating 49-day cycle runs weeks 1–6 followed by Week 0. Week 0 contains the previous season's Trial and promotion event while preparing the next season.

content.heading: Outside societies
content.body: Outside societies host occasional standalone invitationals rather than fully simulated leagues. Visitors may later enter FYI, but external results grant neither direct placement nor FYI Prestige. Outside awards are separate recognition; FYI remains the home society.

content.heading: Career records
content.body: League news and career histories in Generations derive from actual simulated results rather than invented accomplishments. Rivalries, partnerships, dagger provenance and standings persist across the simulation.

content.heading: Partnerships
content.body: Pair chemistry is persistent in the simulation and improves through playing together, not merely winning. Partners chosen for outside events do not override randomly assigned Bold teams.

articles.title: Dragon’s Ascension playoffs
articles.description: Six competitors per division qualify for the playoffs, except Obsidian, which supplies eight. Across eight stages, higher divisions enter progressively and seeding pairs high against low. Playoff results do not govern division movement.

articles.title: FYI Guilds Season 1
articles.description: FYI Guilds Season 1 begins November 22, 2026, and spans nine weeks.

content.heading: Schedule
content.body: Weeks 1–4: regular season. Week 5: Christmas special. Weeks 6–7: regular season. Week 8: The Convergence. Week 9: Championship Final.

content.heading: Format
content.body: Regular events use four rounds. Only finalized results count toward official standings. The Christmas event is a seasonal special rather than a permanent fixture.

articles.title: Guild Championship
articles.description: The Guild Championship is the season-ending contest between the two highest-ranked guilds.

content.heading: Season 1 format
content.body: The finalists nominate five players each for best-of-five head-to-head competition. Each matchup compares the competitors’ four-round totals. The Championship determines the season champion rather than adding regular-season standings points.

articles.title: Guild placement scoring
articles.description: Regular-season FYI Guilds scoring uses two placement brackets based on cumulative raw scores.

content.heading: Brackets
content.body: The six best finishers in each guild form the first bracket; finishers seven through twelve form the second. Lower totals rank higher. The first bracket awards 20, 16, 12, 8, 4 and 2 points; the second awards 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 and 1. Ties split occupied placement points and round each share up.

articles.title: Ignition
articles.description: Ignition is the gateway to the Ladder of Legends, outside the six kingdoms. It has no permanent division or patron dragon.

content.heading: Philosophy
content.body: Its traditional words are “Where Sparks Become Flame.” Ignition offers a beginning regardless of past reputation, success or failure. Where Ash represents recovery, Ignition represents the opportunity to begin.

content.heading: Location and registration
content.body: Ignition takes place in Sparkhaven at the First Forge. Competitors register their names and origins, receive a starting time and a blank Ignition dagger, and have their dagger personalized by a daggersmith.

content.heading: Qualification
content.body: The literary competition uses open seeding followed by head-to-head qualification among sixteen contenders, with eight advancing to Ash. Scores do not carry into Ash.

content.heading: Generations
content.body: The simulation uses Ignition as an open feeder. Its top two promote to Ash, with additional advancement possible when vacancies arise. This game format is distinct from the literary format.

articles.title: Inter-Society Ryder Cup
articles.description: Two twelve-player societies contest twenty-eight matches over three days: eight foursomes, eight four-ball and twelve singles. A win earns one point and a tie half a point; 14.5 wins outright. Eight automatic qualifiers must have participated in the latest Trial, joined by four captain's picks. Captaincy rotates and may be playing or non-playing. The design targets one Cup every two to three seasons, never before a completed Trial. The inaugural 14–14 tie triggers a deciding match; later ties favor the defending society. Captains select willing replacements.

articles.title: Ironbound Arena
articles.description: The standalone Ironbound Arena forms Bold matches immediately among genuine eligible simulated golfers rather than creating queues, fabricated opponents or pending escrow. It has a five-completed-match daily cap, randomized two-on-two play and serialized wager histories. Direct Challenges remain a real FYI bot function outside this arena.

articles.title: Ironbound Ranking
articles.description: Ironbound Ranking totals the five best eligible current-season non-playoff daggers and a separate sixth playoff dagger. The ranking freezes when playoffs conclude.

articles.title: Kharadon’s Ascension
articles.description: Kharadon’s Ascension is the name associated with the literary competitive era spanning Season I and Season II. It is distinct from the mythic destination of Kharadon’s Summit.

content.heading: Seasons
content.body: Season I precedes the present era of The First Spark. Season II is associated with head-to-head competition. Their relationship to the real FYI league formats is not assumed to be identical.

articles.title: Ladder of Legends
articles.description: The Ladder of Legends is Aetherforge’s competitive path from Ignition through the six kingdoms toward Kharadon’s Summit.

content.heading: Origins
content.body: In foundational tradition, Kharadon proposes successive trials as an alternative to the dragons’ rivalry and war. Each kingdom embodies a distinct philosophy of worthiness.

content.heading: Progression
content.body: Competitors begin at Ignition and advance through Ash, Cinder, Ember, Damascus, Titanium and Obsidian. Kharadon’s Summit lies beyond the ordinary divisions.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: Golf is the principal competitive pursuit. Advancement is earned through performance; the Ladder’s traditions reject the notion that former champions own future crowns.

articles.title: Postseason Division Challenges
articles.description: After automatic movement, a challenger stakes original daggers from the target division numbering the division gap plus one. Two-round aggregate decides the match, with ties favoring the defender. A losing challenger returns the staked daggers; a winner retains them and swaps divisions. Auto-relegated competitors, non-division entrants and Trial participants cannot issue challenges. Each issuer and target may participate once, and cannot occupy both roles. Priority is based on qualifying daggers, division and placement.

articles.title: The Convergence
articles.description: The Convergence is a cooperative FYI Guilds event held in week eight of Season 1.

content.heading: Scoring
content.body: Guilds are ranked by combined relative-to-par scores from complete four-round results. Placement points are 40, 30, 20, 16, 12 and 8. These points double if the Council declares the Convergence successful. No numerical success threshold has been finalized in the available rules.

articles.title: The Eight
articles.description: The Eight is the collective designation for Rheon Valek, Nyra Solvar, Sera Voss, Kaelen Rhyne, Mira Ardyn, Torrick Drake, Tessa Brann and Aeren Vale, the group of qualifiers associated with the First Spark era.

articles.title: Trial of Blades
articles.description: The eight highest Prestige competitors qualify across the league, with cutoff ties eligible for play-ins to reduce the field to eight. There are no division quotas. Matches are private eighteen-hole match play without wagers or Bloodied progression. Seeding tiebreaks are playoff showing, regular placement, head-to-head results, dagger count and server tenure.

content.heading: Generations implementation design
content.body: The standalone game schedules the eight actual qualifiers in a seven-day Week 0 bracket after cutoff play-ins. Wagering and Bloodied progression are excluded.

articles.title: Dagger provenance
articles.description: Dagger provenance is the recorded identity, ownership and history of a dagger.

content.heading: League
content.body: Serialized daggers preserve their ownership chains, transfers and enhancements.

content.heading: The Daggersmith game
content.body: Repair and reforging preserve identity where possible; a near-total replacement creates a linked successor rather than a false historical record.

articles.title: Daggersmithing
articles.description: Daggersmithing is the craft of making, engraving and maintaining competitive daggers in Aetherforge. Skilled smiths may also forge golf irons.

content.heading: Work
content.body: Daggersmiths personalize Division Daggers, maintain competitive equipment and may forge irons. Engravings and records preserve a dagger’s identity and competitive history.

articles.title: Enchantments
articles.description: Enchantments are exceptional magical properties associated with equipment. Magic is rare in Aetherforge; no universal mechanism for enchanted equipment has been established.

content.heading: The Daggersmith game
content.body: Rare properties may arise during forging or use and may remain hidden until discovered. This is a game system, not proof of a specific literary enchantment mechanism.

articles.title: Forging stages
articles.description: The Daggersmith game organizes the forging process into five stages.

content.heading: Stages
content.body: Design and materials; forging; refinement and heat treatment; assembly; finishing and appraisal. These are game systems, not a universal historical manufacturing sequence.

articles.title: Irons
articles.description: Irons are crafted golf clubs used by competitors throughout Aetherforge.

content.heading: Notable examples
content.body: Lilith Vanthe’s self-forged irons have obsidian heads, golden shafts and ordinary leather grips. Rowden Groves uses Cinderian brimstone heads and bronze shafts. The exact material properties and any enchantment mechanisms remain unknown.

articles.title: Obsidian (material)
articles.description: Obsidian is a material found alongside basalt in the volcanic landscape around Sparkhaven and used in the heads of forged golf irons. Its precise material properties are not established in the lore.

articles.title: Competitive aliases
articles.description: Before FYI, sporting aliases are the norm. The later Council adds personal and family names alongside aliases to improve transparency and accountability.

articles.title: Guild membership
articles.description: Guild membership in FYI Guilds persists across seasons. Roster changes, participation requirements and release decisions are governed by the applicable season rules.

content.heading: Season 1
content.body: Guilds have a roster limit of fifteen. Leaders may release members after the season for insufficient participation.

articles.title: Hall of Works
articles.description: The Hall of Works is a planned Daggersmith game feature combining a physical display with an illustrated catalogue of notable daggers, including pieces retained or sold.

articles.title: Material culture
articles.description: Aetherforge’s material culture is medieval in character, with smithcraft, stone construction, animal transport and rare magic.

articles.title: Regional dynasties
articles.description: Regional dynasties are the Houses and local institutions of Aetherforge. Some exercise hereditary influence, while others gain standing through craft, public service, commerce or competitive achievement.

content.heading: Regional organization
content.body: Ash is associated with Houses Vale and Mourn and the Greyhands; Cinder with Houses Drake and Mordane and the Ironbound; Ember with Houses Flare and Solvar and the Kindled; Damascus with Houses Ardyn and Velora and the Thousand Hands; Titanium with Houses Rhyne and Calix and the Sentinel Order; Obsidian with Houses Voss, Noirren and Vex.

content.heading: Governance
content.body: These local institutions are distinct from the realm-wide Administrative Council. Their exact jurisdictions are not finalized.

articles.title: The Six Kingdoms
articles.description: Aetherforge’s six kingdoms are Ash, Cinder, Ember, Damascus, Titanium and Obsidian. Each is associated with a dragon and a distinct philosophy.

content.heading: The kingdoms
content.body: Ash: Veyrath, recovery. Cinder: Drakhar, persistence. Ember: Pyrakon, ambition. Damascus: Seraphyne, mastery through creation. Titanium: Aurelith, precision. Obsidian: Varkyros, dominion.

content.heading: The Ladder
content.body: Ignition is a gateway outside the six kingdoms, not a seventh kingdom. Kharadon’s Summit lies beyond the ordinary Ladder. A person’s birthplace and current competitive division are distinct.

articles.title: Ascension Bridges
articles.description: Ascension Bridges are ancient, permanent passages at fixed locations that connect distant parts of Aetherforge.

content.heading: Travel
content.body: The bridges compress distance without eliminating the act of travel. People physically walk across them and emerge at designated arrival points. Their illuminated structures pass through mist and clouds.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The bridges connect kingdoms and form part of the infrastructure of the Ladder. Their ancient origins and full workings remain uncertain.

articles.title: Ash
articles.description: Ash is the first of the six kingdoms on the Ladder of Legends, associated with Veyrath and the ideal of recovery after ruin.

content.heading: Landscape
content.body: Pale forests, ruined towers, waterfalls and new construction stand together. Travelers from Ignition arrive at a broad black stone platform overlooking the ruins. A road descends toward a course that incorporates the remains of older structures.

content.heading: Culture and tradition
content.body: Veyrath’s creed, “Where Ruin Becomes Resolve,” expresses the choice to rebuild and rise after failure. Ash’s identity is founded on resilience rather than poverty or defeat.

articles.title: Aurelion
articles.description: Aurelion is identified in the current geographical outline as the center of Titanium.

articles.title: Brazenhold
articles.description: Brazenhold is identified in the current geographical outline as the center of Cinder.

articles.title: Cinder
articles.description: Cinder is the second kingdom of the Ladder of Legends, associated with Drakhar and the ideal of persistence.

content.heading: Tradition
content.body: Cinder’s philosophy emphasizes endurance, discipline and the capacity to withstand prolonged pressure. Its heraldry includes a hammer on a coal-red shield.

articles.title: Crown Grounds
articles.description: The Crown Grounds are the ceremonial arena within Vaelorian Citadel.

content.heading: Architecture and purpose
content.body: Terraces descend through plazas, galleries and stone courts toward a central arena and dais. The grounds host champions, challengers, delegations and major ceremonies.

articles.title: Damascus
articles.description: Damascus is the fourth kingdom of the Ladder of Legends, associated with Seraphyne and mastery through creation.

content.heading: Tradition
content.body: Seraphyne’s creed is “Craftsmanship. Artistry. Pride.” Damascus values design, forging, artistry and mastery as expressions of strength.

articles.title: Ember
articles.description: Ember is the third kingdom of the Ladder of Legends, associated with Pyrakon and the ideal of ambition.

content.heading: Tradition
content.body: Ember’s philosophy emphasizes momentum, aspiration and the refusal to remain still.

articles.title: Ember Ridge
articles.description: Ember Ridge is associated with Ember in accounts of the kingdom’s geography. Its precise character and boundaries remain uncertain.

articles.title: Hall of the Six
articles.description: The Hall of the Six is the Council chamber at Vaelorian Citadel.

content.heading: Seating
content.body: Five seats face the Founder’s Seat, which denotes the Founder’s leadership rather than hereditary monarchy.

articles.title: Kharadon’s Summit
articles.description: The Summit is the ultimate destination of Ascension in the foundational mythology. The ordinary seven lessons culminate in Obsidian’s Reign; Ascend is associated with Kharadon beyond them.

articles.title: Morrowfall
articles.description: Morrowfall is identified in the current geographical outline as the center of Ash.

articles.title: Nocthar
articles.description: Nocthar, known as the Black Crown, is identified in the current geographical outline as the center of Obsidian.

articles.title: Obsidian
articles.description: Obsidian is the highest ordinary kingdom of the Ladder of Legends, associated with Varkyros and dominion.

content.heading: Tradition
content.body: Obsidian’s philosophy concerns sovereignty and the capacity to retain command under pressure. Kharadon’s Summit lies beyond the ordinary divisions.

articles.title: Serathis
articles.description: Serathis, known as the City of a Thousand Forges, is identified in the current geographical outline as the center of Damascus.

articles.title: Sparkhaven
articles.description: Sparkhaven is the gateway settlement of Ignition, approached by an Ascension Bridge that arrives outside its walls.

content.heading: Landscape and architecture
content.body: Basalt, obsidian and black volcanic walls characterize the approach. Above the entrance stands the motto “Every Legend Begins With a Spark.” The landscape is warm and dry beneath an orange sky.

content.heading: Life and competition
content.body: Crowded streets, forge lamps, mule carts, taverns and competitor lodgings serve the settlement. Horns mark the opening of the gates, and an avenue descends toward the First Forge. Registration takes place under awnings overlooking the course.

articles.title: The First Ascension Bridge
articles.description: The First Ascension Bridge connects Ignition with Ash, reaching the black stone landing overlooking Ash’s ruins.

articles.title: The First Forge
articles.description: The First Forge is the principal competition course of Ignition, located at Sparkhaven.

content.heading: Landscape
content.body: The grounds wind through volcanic ridges, dark stone, towers, streams and long grass. Elevated tees, canyons and uneven winds demand judgment and accuracy.

content.heading: Facilities
content.body: The grounds contain practice areas, a scoring pavilion and spectator areas. Beneath the course is an older control chamber containing stone records and metal housings. Its origin and full function remain uncertain.

articles.title: Titanium
articles.description: Titanium is the fifth kingdom of the Ladder of Legends, associated with Aurelith and precision.

content.heading: Tradition
content.body: Its philosophy values preparation, control and repeatable mastery.

articles.title: Vaelorian Citadel
articles.description: Vaelorian Citadel is Aetherforge’s neutral capital and ceremonial center, outside the sovereignty of the ordinary divisions.

content.heading: Architecture
content.body: Its silver and black spires rise above the mist, linked by illuminated bridges. Kharadon’s Summit is visible beyond the Citadel.

content.heading: Institutions
content.body: The Citadel houses the Administrative Council, archives and the Crown Grounds, where major competitive ceremonies take place.

articles.title: Age of Ascendants
articles.description: The Age of Ascendants describes the period in which the Ladder became institutionalized. Academies, Houses, divisional competitions, ceremonial honors and rival schools of golf developed around it.

articles.title: Age of Champions
articles.description: The Age of Champions is a historical designation for the era of legendary contenders following the First Ascension and preceding the Broken Summit. Its precise chronological boundaries remain unsettled.

articles.title: Age of Six Wings
articles.description: The six dragon philosophies define the recorded mythology of this age: Veyrath’s recovery, Drakhar’s persistence, Pyrakon’s ambition, Seraphyne’s mastery through creation, Aurelith’s precision and Varkyros’s dominion.

articles.title: Age of the First Spark
articles.description: The creation traditions describe the primordial elemental storm, the emergence of the First Spark and its association with the Eternal Forge. The Forge is said to respond to struggle and determination. These accounts form a mythological foundation, not a confirmed dated chronology.

articles.title: Darian's Ascension
articles.description: Darian Vex’s ascent is associated with his challenge to Kharadon’s authority over Summit access. Historical accounts describe a reform grievance that eventually developed into a struggle for supremacy.

articles.title: First Ascension
articles.description: The First Ascension is the legendary achievement of Kael Varen, remembered as the first contender to complete the Ladder and reach Kharadon’s Summit. Traditional accounts say he returned; its exact date remains unknown.

articles.title: Ladder Awakening
articles.description: The Ladder Awakening is a documented instance of extraordinary activity in ancient infrastructure across the six kingdoms and toward the Summit. Its underlying cause is unknown.

articles.title: Lost Kael Period
articles.description: The Lost Kael Period refers to the disputed history following Kael Varen’s First Ascension. Traditions diverge about his disappearance, death, return or silence; no single account is definitive.

articles.title: Reforging
articles.description: The Reforging is remembered as the restoration of the Ladder and its bridges after the Broken Summit. Competition resumes as damaged infrastructure and institutions are rebuilt.

articles.title: Sanitization of History
articles.description: The sanitization of history refers to the simplification and alteration of historical accounts surrounding Kael Varen, Darian Vex, Kharadon and the Ladder after the Reforging. The relative roles of deliberate suppression and ordinary cultural mythmaking remain unresolved.

articles.title: Second Descent
articles.description: The Second Descent is a mysterious historical reference discovered in an old access record dating thirty-one years after Kael Varen’s first ascent. The record preserves identifier 117-3A but does not identify the individual by name.

articles.title: War of the Broken Summit
articles.description: The Broken Summit is a historical conflict associated with Darian Vex and the Crownless.

content.heading: Aftermath
content.body: The conflict damaged the relationship between the realm’s institutions and the movement. Crownless ideas survived despite the defeat; the precise historical circumstances remain disputed.

articles.title: War of the Six Crowns
articles.description: The six dragons are said to have contested competing philosophies of worthiness without any achieving absolute victory. Whether the dragons fought directly, through kingdoms or both remains disputed.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: The War of the Six Crowns began over competing philosophies of worthiness, not territory alone. Traditional accounts describe burned mountains, shattered fortresses, lost cities and fractured floating continents. No dragon won absolutely. Kharadon initially withheld intervention so the Six could learn their philosophies’ limits, then acted when their conflict endangered the Eternal Forge. The account has him issue a challenge rather than attack, replacing their war with successive trials of all six philosophies.

articles.title: Ignition: The First Spark
articles.description: Ignition: The First Spark is the opening work of the Aetherforge saga, centered on Aeren Vale and the entry stage of the Ladder of Legends.

articles.title: Saga of Aetherforge
articles.description: The Saga of Aetherforge is the planned literary series organized around Ignition, the six kingdoms and Kharadon’s Summit.

content.heading: Current working titles
content.body: Ignition: The First Spark; Ash: Where Ruin Becomes Resolve; Cinder: The Unyielding; Ember: Feed the Flame; Damascus: The Queen’s Forge; Titanium: The Silver Measure; Obsidian: The Black Crown; Kharadon’s Summit: Every Legend Must Ascend. The later titles and final volume structure remain provisional.

articles.title: The Daggersmith (game)
articles.description: The Daggersmith is a smithcraft game set in Aetherforge. Players develop a novice smith through commissions, craft mastery and mentorship, with the aim of becoming the Daggersmith’s apprentice and craft successor.

content.heading: Craft
content.body: Gameplay centers on forging, materials, commissions, workmanship, reputation and mentorship.

content.heading: World
content.body: Damascus is the fixed beta origin; the broader design envisages origins across all six kingdoms. Craft succession is distinct from inheriting Lilith’s Council office.

articles.title: The Daggersmith (literary work)
articles.description: The Daggersmith is a prequel centered on Lilith Vanthe’s early career as a smith and golfer, before the modern Council era.

articles.title: The Summit and the Chain
articles.description: The Summit and the Chain is a work attributed to Darian Vex concerning authority and access to Kharadon’s Summit.

articles.title: Aether
articles.description: Aether is associated in Aetherforge’s creation traditions with the primordial elemental storm from which the First Spark emerged. Its origin and precise workings remain uncertain.

articles.title: Ascension infrastructure
articles.description: Ancient infrastructure underlies parts of the Ladder, its bridges and competitive grounds. Older systems survive beneath modern facilities, including the control chamber under the First Forge. Their origins, full purpose and operation remain unknown.

articles.title: Magic
articles.description: Magic exists in Aetherforge but is exceptional rather than a routine part of everyday life. The Ascension Bridges are an established example of magical travel; the mechanisms behind extraordinary craftsmanship and ancient infrastructure remain uncertain.

articles.title: Aurelith
articles.description: Aurelith is associated with Titanium and precision.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: Tradition portrays Aurelith as the foremost battlefield strategist among the divisional dragons and Titanium as a realm of silver fortifications, geometric towers, disciplined armies and precise engineering.

articles.title: Drakhar
articles.description: Drakhar is the dragon associated with Cinder and the ideal of persistence.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: Drakhar’s tradition emphasizes perseverance through exhaustion, failure and adversity.

articles.title: Eternal Forge
articles.description: The Eternal Forge is associated with the First Spark. Myth describes it as responsive to struggle, pressure, conflict and determination.

articles.title: First Spark
articles.description: In Aetherforge’s creation tradition, a point of impossible heat emerged and became the Eternal Forge. The First Spark names this mythic beginning; its account should be read as tradition, not a verified physical explanation.

articles.title: Kharadon
articles.description: Kharadon is revered as King of Dragons and Keeper of the Eternal Forge. His ancient sovereignty stands apart from the six kingdom dragons and the ordinary Ladder hierarchy.

content.heading: Origins
content.body: Traditions disagree on whether Kharadon preceded, discovered or emerged from the Forge. The mythological Age of Kharadon takes its name from him.

content.heading: Role
content.body: The foundational tradition credits Kharadon with proposing the Ladder as an alternative to the dragons’ rivalry. His guardianship of the Forge and Summit is distinct from the Administrative Council’s governance of mortal institutions.

articles.title: Pyrakon
articles.description: Pyrakon is the Flameborn, the dragon of Ember and the ideal of ambition.

content.heading: Philosophy
content.body: His creed is “Feed the Flame.” He values the pursuit of advancement over safe stagnation.

articles.title: Seraphyne
articles.description: Seraphyne is the dragon of Damascus, known as the Queen. She embodies mastery through creation.

content.heading: Philosophy
content.body: Her creed is “Craftsmanship. Artistry. Pride.” She regards design, forging and perfection as expressions of strength.

articles.title: Seven Lessons of Ascension
articles.description: The traditional sequence of lessons is Ignition — Begin; Ash — Rise; Cinder — Endure; Ember — Hunger; Damascus — Master; Titanium — Perfect; and Obsidian — Reign. Ascend belongs to Kharadon beyond the seven stages, rather than constituting another ordinary division.

articles.title: Unshaped Aether
articles.description: The oldest creation traditions describe an elemental storm before the existence of land and sky. The name Unshaped Aether refers to this primordial condition rather than a confirmed historical era.

articles.title: Varkyros
articles.description: Varkyros is associated with Obsidian and dominion.

content.heading: Traditional accounts
content.body: Varkyros is called the Black Sovereign. His creed is recorded as “Forged in Fire.” His tradition emphasizes maintaining command after victory and recognizes Kharadon’s authority beyond the Ladder.

articles.title: Veyrath
articles.description: Veyrath is the dragon of Ash, representing recovery after ruin.

content.heading: Philosophy
content.body: His creed is “Where Ruin Becomes Resolve.” He represents the choice to rise after failure.

articles.title: Administrative Council
articles.description: The Administrative Council is Aetherforge’s principal mortal governing body. It oversees competition, administration and records while ancient dragon authority remains distinct.

content.heading: Formation
content.body: The Council grew from a reform circle formed by Lyra, Bustin and Whiskey in Ember. Lilith joined after meeting Lyra in Cinder; PJ and Soulless joined the circle through their connections in Damascus. The six built influence over years before establishing the Council. By The First Spark, it has existed for approximately fifteen to twenty-five years.

content.heading: Members and responsibilities
content.body: Lyra (Acolyte12), the Founder; Lilith Vanthe (Pretty), the Daggersmith; PJ, the Vaelorian Seer; Bustin, the Forge Engineer; Whiskey, the Aetherforge Sentinel; and Soulless, the Master of the Inferno.

content.heading: Principles
content.body: The Council’s members were accomplished contenders before becoming governors. Its principle is to stand among competitors, not apart from them. Members do not decide matters directly affecting their own competitive interests.

articles.title: Ascendants (Crownless)
articles.description: The Ascendants are the Crownless faction that sought to take the Summit by force.

articles.title: Crownless
articles.description: The Crownless are a movement associated with opposition to dragon authority and the events of the Broken Summit.

content.heading: History
content.body: The earlier movement collapsed following Darian Vex’s defeat, but its ideas and adherents survived. Its factions do not all share identical aims or methods.

content.heading: Symbols
content.body: A vertically split crown and the declaration “No height beyond reach” are associated with the Crownless.

articles.title: FYI
articles.description: FYI is the organization founded by Lyra in the modern era to administer competition and support the community of contenders.

content.heading: Governance
content.body: Its Administrative Council grew from a reform circle of active competitors. The ancient Ladder and Crucibles existed before FYI.

articles.title: FYI Guilds
articles.description: FYI Guilds is a team competition organized around six guilds named for the kingdom dragons: Veyrath, Drakhar, Pyrakon, Seraphyne, Aurelith and Varkyros.

content.heading: Competition
content.body: Guilds earn standings points through regular-event placements, Kingdom Seals and Kharadon’s Crown. The season also includes a cooperative Convergence and a Championship.

content.heading: Roster
content.body: The Season 1 roster limit is fifteen members per guild. Membership persists between seasons.

articles.title: Greyhands
articles.description: The Greyhands are a respected rebuilding and engineering guild associated with Ash. Their influence is not hereditary nobility.

articles.title: Hollow Crown
articles.description: The Hollow Crown is the Crownless faction that sought to destroy dragon sovereignty completely.

articles.title: House Ardyn
articles.description: House Ardyn is associated with Damascus. Known as the Masters of Adaptation, the House values strategy and competitive reinvention. Its motto is PERFECTION MOVES, and Selene Ardyn is associated with its legacy.

articles.title: House Calix
articles.description: House Calix is associated with Titanium. Known as the Keepers of Sequence, it is distinguished by logistics, organization and long-term planning.

articles.title: House Drake
articles.description: House Drake is associated with Cinder. The Long Watch emphasizes endurance, discipline and military service. Associated with Torren Drake, it bears the motto STAND AFTER STANDING FAILS.

articles.title: House Flare
articles.description: House Flare is associated with Ember. The Red Line is a bold, volatile lineage associated with Aric Flare; its motto is HIGHER OR ASH.

content.heading: Overview
content.body: House Flare’s history includes disastrous as well as successful periods; its bold and volatile reputation is not simply unbroken triumph.

articles.title: House Mordane
articles.description: House Mordane, the Wardens of Brazenhold, is a Cinder dynasty associated with defense and military service.

articles.title: House Mourn
articles.description: House Mourn is associated with Ash. Known as the Keepers of Memory, its archivists, historians, memorial keepers and chroniclers uphold the motto NOTHING LOST IS FORGOTTEN.

articles.title: House Noirren
articles.description: House Noirren is associated with Obsidian. The Quiet Crown is distinguished by intelligence, diplomacy, secrets, leverage and political calculation.

articles.title: House Rhyne
articles.description: House Rhyne is associated with Titanium. The Measured Line comprises strategists, judges, planners and champions, and is associated with Caelor Rhyne. Its motto is NOTHING WASTED.

articles.title: House Solvar
articles.description: House Solvar, the Flamecourt, is an influential commercial and competitive family associated with Ember.

content.heading: Overview
content.body: The Flamecourt is described not only as commercially influential but as ambitious, connected and politically sophisticated.

articles.title: House Vale
articles.description: House Vale is associated with Ash. Known as the Rebuilders, it embodies reconstruction and resilience and bears the motto WE RISE AGAIN. Lyra Vale is associated with its legacy, and its crest includes a silver ash-leaf.

articles.title: House Velora
articles.description: House Velora, the Architects of Serathis, is a Damascus lineage associated with art and architecture.

articles.title: House Vex
articles.description: House Vex, the Crownless Line, was once a prestigious Obsidian House. After the Broken Summit the House was politically destroyed, with branches exiled, stripped of position or destroyed. Survivors scattered, adopted new names or severed public lineage.

articles.title: House Voss
articles.description: House Voss is an Obsidian competitive dynasty known as the Black Line. Associated with Malrek Voss, it bears the motto TAKE THE HEIGHT. HOLD IT.

articles.title: Ironbound
articles.description: The Ironbound are a Cinder coalition of veterans, smiths, guards, labor leaders and traditionalists devoted to endurance.

articles.title: Kindled
articles.description: The Kindled are an Ember populist faction that challenges inherited privilege.

articles.title: New Crownless
articles.description: The New Crownless is a contemporary expression of Crownless ideology, questioning authority over the Ladder and access to its highest stages. Its messages include unsigned black cards and the split crown symbol; the extent of its organization remains uncertain.

articles.title: Reformers
articles.description: The Reformers are the Crownless faction that sought greater mortal power and eventually abandoned the rebellion.

articles.title: Sentinel Order
articles.description: Titanium's Sentinel Order is an elite institution whose membership is earned rather than hereditary. It performs military and administrative duties.

articles.title: Smithing licenses
articles.description: Smithing licenses are a proposed professional qualification system in The Daggersmith game. Licensing, revocation and reinstatement are design concepts; the responsible in-world institutions have not been finalized.

articles.title: Thousand Hands
articles.description: The Thousand Hands is a coalition of Damascus master guilds with substantial cultural influence.

articles.title: Calendar of Aetherforge
articles.description: The traditional chronology distinguishes events before the founding of the Ladder (BL) from those after it (AL). Precise dates for much of Aetherforge’s ancient history remain uncertain.

articles.title: Golden Dragons
articles.description: Golden Dragons are a denomination of currency used in Aetherforge.

articles.title: Sorceress Supreme
articles.description: Sorceress Supreme is Lyra’s title as Founder of FYI, associated with vision, identity, direction and legacy. The title does not by itself imply spellcasting.

articles.title: The Daggersmith (title)
articles.description: The Daggersmith is Lilith Vanthe’s Council title. As Dragon’s Ascension Administrator, she oversees divisions, standings, head-to-head competition and competitive daggers.
